title: Early Intensive Developmental and Behavioral Intervention (EIDBI) service authorization timeline update
supports: DHS states its medical review agent Acentra Health is experiencing longer-than-required EIDBI service-authorization timelines because of increased review volume.
DHS and Acentra say they are increasing review capacity, improving workflow efficiency, and prioritizing initial CMDE/ITP cases and renewals at risk of authorization gaps.
DHS states EIDBI authorizations may be retroactively approved up to 180 days, but not beyond that window, and advises providers to submit at least 30 days before intended service start.
does_not_support: The backlog is not itself evidence of fraud by providers or recipients.
The source does not quantify the number of delayed authorizations or affected children.
The source does not establish that program-integrity review is the sole cause of increased review volume.
source_locator: MHCP provider news lines 150-187 as retrieved 2026-08-29
